about.title: Commerce Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Commerce is a working city, packed with warehouses, distribution centers, and industrial yards near I-5 and Telegraph Road, which means residents come into contact with machinery, tools, vehicles, and consumer goods every single day. When one of those products fails because of a flaw in its design, a manufacturing mistake, or a missing warning label, the person hurt is rarely at fault, yet they're often left with medical bills and lost wages. California law recognizes this and allows injured people to pursue compensation from manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without having to prove anyone was careless. We don't take a cut of any settlement; we handle product liability claims and explain your options plainly. If you were hurt by something that should have worked as intended, it's worth having us look at what happened before you talk to an insurer.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally lets injured people show a product was defective and caused harm without proving the maker was negligent. We can help identify whether the defect was in design, manufacturing, or warning.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can all be liable under California product liability law. That matters in a city like Commerce with heavy warehouse and distribution activity.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Because the product itself is often the key piece of evidence, holding onto it (rather than discarding or repairing it) can make a real difference. We can advise you on safely storing it while your claim moves forward.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product at a warehouse job near Telegraph Road. Can I still file a claim?
items.answer: Possibly — a workplace injury from a defective product may involve both a workers' compensation claim and a separate product liability claim against the manufacturer. These are different legal paths, so it's worth having us review both angles.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No. California product liability generally uses strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone was negligent. This can make these claims more approachable than some other injury cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it, if you safely can, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions. The product itself is often central evidence in these claims, and we can guide you on how to preserve it properly.
